'''''Gastridium ventricosum''''' is a species of [[Poaceae|grass]] known by the common name '''nit-grass''' (British Isles)<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> or '''nit grass''' (USA).<ref>{{cite web |title=Plants Profile for ''Gastridium ventricosum'' (nit grass) |url=https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=GAPH2 |publisher=USDA |work=Plants Database |access-date=2015-02-16 }}</ref> This is an annual grass bearing a long, thin, smooth inflorescence of spikelets. It is native to Europe, North Africa, and southwestern Asia but has become naturalized in scattered locations elsewhere.<ref name=j>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=417490 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>[https://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/cgi-bin/get_JM_treatment.pl?Gastridium%20ventricosum Jepson Manual Treatment]</ref><ref>[https://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=gastridium+ventricosum Altervista Flora Italiana, Codino maggiore, Nit Grass,  ''Gastridium ventricosum'' (Gouan) Schinz & Thell. ]</ref>
